findings.title: Date-override early return skips the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body: When a slot falls on a day with a date override and is not rejected by the range checks, `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` returns before the `busy.every(...)` block. Bookings, calendar busy times and buffers are therefore never consulted for that host on override days. A fixed host with an override can be offered a slot that overlaps an existing booking or calendar event. This applies to every personal and collective event too, since those hosts are all treated as fixed. The override should only decide whether the slot is inside working time, and the busy check should still run afterwards.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects slots for any user with several ranges on the same day
findings.body: `workingHours.find(...)` returns true, meaning "outside working hours", as soon as the slot is outside any single working-hour entry that includes today. `getWorkingHours` yields one entry per distinct start/end range, so a user with 9-12 and 13-17 on Mon-Fri has two entries covering the same days. A slot at 10:00 is inside the first entry but outside the second, so the whole slot is rejected. Because personal and collective hosts are `isFixed`, every user with a split schedule, such as a lunch break, would now lose all their slots. The check must pass if the slot is inside at least one entry (`some`/`every` with the logic inverted), not fail if it is outside any one.

findings.title: `end` in the working-hours check is computed from the slot start, not the slot end
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` only tests the slot's start. A slot that starts inside working hours but runs past the end (for example a 60-minute slot at 16:30 with working hours ending at 17:00) is treated as available. It should use `slotEndTime` (start plus event length).

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day make slots unavailable
findings.body: The override check uses `find`, which returns true ("slot not within override") if the slot is outside any one override whose day matches. A user can have several override ranges on one date, for example 9-12 and 14-17. A slot at 10:00 is inside the first range but before the second, so the second range returns true and the slot is rejected. A slot is only outside the overrides when it is outside all of them for that day. The check should be an `every`/`some` over the day's overrides, not a short-circuit on the first miss.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with `===` so the zero-length override branch never fires
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references, which is always false, so this branch is dead code. The intent was to detect a zero-length (fully unavailable) override. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()`.

findings.title: Override day compared via server-local formatting against UTC slot day
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').format('YYYY MM DD')` formats in the server's local timezone, but it is compared with `slotStartTime.format(...)`, which is UTC. On any server whose TZ is not UTC (local dev, some deployments) the day match can be off by one and silently apply or skip overrides. Even in UTC, matching on the UTC calendar day rather than the organizer's calendar day misassigns overrides near midnight, for example a 02:00-05:00 IST override that lies on the previous UTC day. Both sides should be formatted in the same explicit timezone, normally the organizer's.

findings.title: Override day filter and time-of-day wrap are not adjusted for the new timezone offset
findings.body: The new offset is applied to the override's hour and minute, but `activeOverrides` still picks overrides by comparing the unshifted `override.start` to the invitee's day boundaries. An override can therefore be assigned to the wrong invitee day. Example: organizer wall-clock 20:00 and invitee +6:00. The offset is also applied via `.hour() * 60 + .minute()`, which wraps modulo 24h. An override that shifts across midnight gets a start and end on different days, so `end < start`. `buildSlots` then drops it as invalid or places it on the wrong day. The shifted range needs to be mapped to the correct invitee day and split or clamped at midnight.

findings.title: `override.start.toString()` and optional `timeZone` used for offset calculation
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` goes through `Date.toString()`, which is locale and format dependent and drops milliseconds; pass the `Date` directly. `override.timeZone` is optional in the `TimeRange` type, and `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the server's guessed zone. Any caller that does not set `timeZone` silently gets a wrong offset (or zero) instead of the old behaviour. There should be a fallback to `organizerTimeZone` or an explicit skip when it is missing.

findings.title: Tests do not cover the main fix (fixed-host date overrides) and the new timezone test is weak
findings.body: The PR's headline fix is that a fixed host's date override restricts round-robin slots. No test creates a round-robin event with a fixed host and an override, and none covers split working hours, multiple overrides per day, or an override day with busy bookings. Those are exactly the cases where the new `checkIfIsAvailable` logic breaks. The added Dhaka test only asserts the same UTC slots as the IST case. The custom `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher iterates only over the actual slots and never checks the length, so missing expected slots would still pass.
